Even if work is okay, I start worrying about the boiler breaking, or my blood pressure, or that I’ll end up alone and helpless like some of the elderly clients I clean for. After my husband died a few years ago, life definitely got harder, but this worrying feels bigger than just that. It’s in everything, every day.

Sometimes I’m cleaning a bathroom and I realize I’ve wiped the same spot three times because I’m lost in my head, playing out worst‑case scenarios. I can’t concentrate, and I feel tense all the time, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen, even when nothing particular is wrong.
